title: NSLC Business & Entrepreneurship
description: NSLC's Business & Entrepreneurship program is a nine-day residential summer program held on university campuses in which high school students role-play launching and running a company from scratch. The core curriculum includes a business-pitch exercise where student teams develop a new product or service and present it for feedback from real Inc. 5000 entrepreneurs, a separate management simulation covering finance, marketing, operations, and product R&D decisions, an industry-analysis exercise evaluating competing businesses, and a 'Social Media Madness' branding/PR module. All NSLC high-school tracks also share a common leadership curriculum (communication styles, resilience, empathy) and professional-development sessions on networking, resume-building, interviewing, and public speaking. Instruction is led by industry professionals and guest speakers, including past Inc. 5000 CEOs. In summer 2026 the program ran at four campuses -- Columbia University, Duke University, UC Berkeley, and the University of Michigan -- for $4,195-$4,495 depending on location; as of this research, NSLC's site had not yet posted 2027 dates or locations, instead inviting students to 'sign up for early access to Summer 2027.'
selectivity_evidence: No published acceptance rate or competitive review process found. NSLC states it 'encourages all... students who demonstrate academic excellence and leadership ability to apply,' and enrollment proceeds via online application and deposit rather than a described selective admissions review -- consistent with a paid enrollment program rather than a competitively selective one.

title: Future Makers: An NYU Stern Pre-College Institute
description: Future Makers is a five-day, in-person, non-residential pre-college institute at NYU Stern School of Business in Greenwich Village for students in grades 9-12. The week centers on one sustained business simulation: student teams analyze information about a fictional company, evaluate strategic opportunities, and develop and present recommendations addressing a business challenge, working across areas including strategy, financial analysis, customer insight, and leadership communication. Teaching combines faculty-led sessions and hands-on activities with near-peer mentoring from NYU Stern graduate and undergraduate student leaders, who guide team discussions and give feedback. The August 2026 institute (August 3-7, $650 per student) was directed by Adjunct Associate Professor John Hopkins with curriculum advisor Julian Yeo, Deputy Chair & Clinical Professor in Stern's Department of Accounting. Registration for that session has since closed, and NYU Stern's page did not yet list a 2027 date as of this research.
selectivity_evidence: No published acceptance rate or competitive admissions review found; the program uses paid online registration (2026: $650) rather than a described selective application process, and registration status was tracked simply as open/closed rather than admit/deny.
